title: Impact of wind turbine noise on health: a blind spot in EU green policy
text:
QUESTION

PE782.736v01-00
Question for written answer E-000019/2026
to the Commission
Rule 144
Virginie Joron (PfE)
Subject:
Impact of wind turbine noise on health: a blind spot in EU green policy
Until now, accurately measuring the noise generated by wind turbines has been difficult.
However, on 12 November 2025, a study carried out by Uppsala University in Sweden
presented a high-fidelity simulation tool for more accurate acoustic modelling1. The results
show that ‘modern, large-scale wind turbines generate infrasound levels significantly higher
than those reported for older, smaller turbines.’
However, the current legal framework, and especially Directive 2002/49/EC relating to the
assessment and management of environmental noise, does not take into account this new
scientific data2.
1.
In light of these new scientific findings, does the Commission intend to revise Directive
2002/49/EC relating to the assessment and management of environmental noise in order
to include the effects of infrasound emitted by wind turbines?
2.
Does the Commission plan to support research, including through EU-funded
programmes, aimed at developing instruments allowing noise and infrasound pollution
linked to wind turbines to be measured and proven?
3.
Does the Commission intend to impose harmonised thresholds at EU level for noise and
infrasound emissions, given the potential impact of these emissions on public health
among people living nearby?
Submitted: 6.1.2026

--- ANSWER ---

(English version)
Question for written answer E-000019/26
to the Commission
Virginie Joron (PfE)
(6 January 2026)
Subject: Impact of wind turbine noise on health: a blind spot in EU green policy
Until now, accurately measuring the noise generated by wind turbines has been difficult. However, on 12 November 2025, a
study carried out by Uppsala University in Sweden presented a high-fidelity simulation tool for more accurate acoustic
modelling (1). The results show that ‘modern, large-scale wind turbines generate infrasound levels significantly higher than
those reported for older, smaller turbines.’
However, the current legal framework, and especially Directive 2002/49/EC relating to the assessment and management of
environmental noise, does not take into account this new scientific data (2).
1.
In light of these new scientific findings, does the Commission intend to revise Directive 2002/49/EC relating to the
assessment and management of environmental noise in order to include the effects of infrasound emitted by wind turbines?
2.
Does the Commission plan to support research, including through EU-funded programmes, aimed at developing
instruments allowing noise and infrasound pollution linked to wind turbines to be measured and proven?
3.
Does the Commission intend to impose harmonised thresholds at EU level for noise and infrasound emissions, given the
potential impact of these emissions on public health among people living nearby?
Submitted: 6.1.2026
Answer given by Ms Roswall on behalf of the European Commission
(18 February 2026)
The Environmental Noise Directive (END) (1) is the main EU legislative instrument for addressing excessive noise pollution
mainly caused by transport traffic, as well as from industrial activities listed in Annex I of the Industrial Emissions Directive
(IED) (2).
As electricity generation from wind turbines is not listed in the Annex I of IED, there are no specific noise requirements for
them under the END.
Wind projects (3) are subject to an Environmental Impact Assessment (4) before authorisation, which includes a description of
the emission of noise, and of the measures envisaged to prevent, reduce or, if possible, offset any adverse effect.
Member States are required, every five years, to adopt strategic noise maps showing noise exposure from major sources (5). In
this process, the END refers to the use of A-weighted equivalent sound levels as primary regulatory metrics in line with the
guidelines of the World Health Organisation (WHO) (6).
It is however noted that wind turbines generate infrasound or lower frequencies of sound than traffic sources which may not be
fully addressed by standard noise metrics.
As outlined in 2023 Implementation Report (7) and the Zero Pollution Mid-Term Review (8), the Commission is committed to
improving the implementation of the END.

In the EU programme for the environment and climate action (9), noise and vibrations from wind turbines is a priority topic (10)
and in Horizon Europe (11) several projects have investigated noise from wind turbines (12). The Commission has also accepted
the recommendations of the European Court of Auditors (13) to assess the feasibility of introducing EU noise-reduction targets
and noise limits in the END, and of aligning the noise exposure reporting thresholds as closely as possible with those
recommended by the WHO.
